issues.current: DHS directory lists a 15-hour assisted living administrator training course (directory dated 3/22/2019; current hours not confirmed); cost $300-$1,000
issues.correct: Before initial employment, an administrator must complete (1) a Department-approved and administered orientation, (2) a 100-hour standardized Department-approved administrator training course, and (3) a Department-approved competency test with a passing score. Annual training is then at least 24 hours.
issues.evidence: §2800.64(a)(2): "A 100-hour standardized Department-approved administrator training course." §2800.64(c): "at least 24 hours of annual training relating to the job duties." The DHS copy of Ch. 2800 shows §2800.64 as amended June 2016.
issues.fix: Replace the '15-hour course' language with: orientation + 100-hour course + competency test before hire, and 24 hours of annual training. Re-price the startup line for a 100-hour course (price unverifiable). Add 24 hours of annual administrator training to the training budget. Add 4 hours of dementia training within 30 days of hire and 2 hours annually (§2800.69).

issues.correct: Transportation is a mandatory assisted living service. The residence must provide or arrange transportation on a regular weekly basis for medical and social appointments. If the residence supplies its own vehicle, at least one vehicle must be wheelchair-accessible. It must keep registration, inspection and vehicle insurance records, and the driver must be 18+ and licensed.
issues.evidence: §2800.171(a): "shall be required to provide or arrange for transportation on a regular weekly basis." §2800.220(b)(7) lists transportation among the minimum services. §2800.171(c) requires vehicle insurance documentation. §2800.171(d) requires an accessible vehicle if the residence supplies its own.
issues.fix: Change the note to 'Mandatory (§2800.171, §2800.220(b)(7))'. Budget for an accessible vehicle or a contract transport provider, vehicle insurance, and driver and assistant labor. Cost is an operator estimate.

issues.current: The current ALR nurse requirement was not confirmed (a 2015 compendium says RN in the building or on call; later summaries say licensed nurse)
issues.correct: The requirement is confirmed. The residence must have a licensed nurse available in the building or on call at all times, as an employee or under contract. An LPN under RN supervision, or an RN, must complete or approve the initial assessment, preliminary support plan and final support plan, and review the plan quarterly.
issues.evidence: §2800.60(d): "the residence shall have a licensed nurse available in the building or on call at all times." §2800.227(b): "An LPN, under the supervision of an RN, shall review and approve the final support plan."
issues.fix: State the nurse requirement as confirmed under §2800.60(d). Re-test whether $800/month fixed covers 24/7 on-call coverage plus assessments and quarterly plan reviews, especially for 16 and 40 residents (estimate, unverifiable).

issues.correct: The residence must have a dietitian on staff or under contract for any special dietary needs in a support plan.
issues.evidence: §2800.60(e): "The residence shall have a dietician on staff or under contract to provide for any special dietary needs of a resident as indicated in his support plan."
issues.fix: Add a fixed opex line 'Contracted dietitian' (amount unverifiable; get quotes) to all ALR configurations.

issues.correct: Pennsylvania's Workers' Compensation Act requires employers with employees to carry workers' compensation insurance (77 P.S. §501, Section 305). Treat it as a mandatory cost. The 4% rate is unverifiable.
issues.evidence: I did not fetch a primary source for this. It is based on the PA Workers' Compensation Act, which L&I administers.
issues.fix: Change the note to 'Mandatory for any employer with employees.' Get a quote under the nursing and residential care class code, because 4% of payroll is unverifiable and may be low for direct-care labor.

issues.current: alr6: no cook, housekeeping or laundry hours. alr16: 260 hrs/month described as 'about 15 hrs/week housekeeping plus 40 hrs/week cook'.
issues.correct: Food service (3 meals plus snacks daily), housekeeping, laundry (weekly linen change) and a daily activities program are mandatory services, and staffing must cover them. 55 hrs/week is about 238 hrs/month, not 260.
issues.evidence: §2800.60(c): "Additional staff hours, or contractual hours, shall be provided as necessary to meet the transportation, laundry, food service, housekeeping and maintenance needs." §2800.220(b) lists meals, laundry, housekeeping and activities. §2800.105(d) requires weekly linen changes.
issues.fix: Add a cook/housekeeping/laundry labor line to alr6_private, or state explicitly that the 730 direct-care hours absorb it (which then conflicts with the added service-time line). In alr16 either correct 260 to about 238 or correct the note to about 60 hrs/week, and add explicit laundry hours.

issues.current: Accessibility and physical plant upgrades $5,000-$100,000 (operator estimate; only the 225 sq ft rule mentioned)
issues.correct: Unit-level mandatory features are not itemized. Each resident gets their own living unit (sharing only by written voluntary agreement, max 2). Each unit needs its own bathroom (toilet, sink, tub/shower, grab bars), an emergency notification system in the unit and the bathroom, a lockable door, a telephone jack, an individually controlled thermostat, and a window. Central air conditioning is required for new construction. Two wheelchair-accessible common rooms are required, plus an AED in each building and a public restroom.
issues.evidence: §2800.101(a),(b)(3),(h),(r); §2800.102(a)-(d),(n),(m); §2800.98(a); §2800.83(c); §2800.96(a): "The residence shall have an automatic external defibrillation device located in each building."
issues.fix: Itemize per-unit private bathrooms, call systems, thermostats, central A/C, AED(s) and ADA-compliant public restroom in startup costs. Re-test the 6-bed converted-house case, since it needs six units each with a bathroom. The cost amounts are unverifiable.

issues.current: Only dated sources were found: a 2015 compendium (18 hours) and a 2019 summary (16 hours annual). Check the current Ch. 2800 training section.
issues.correct: Direct care staff may not provide unsupervised assisted living services until they complete 18 hours of training and pass the competency test. They need first aid and CPR certification before providing care, an orientation within 40 scheduled working hours, and 16 hours of annual training. Dementia training is 4 hours within 30 days and 2 hours annually, in addition to those hours.
issues.evidence: §2800.65(g): "may not provide unsupervised assisted living services until completion of 18 hours of training". §2800.65(h): "at least 16 hours of annual training". §2800.65(c): certified in first aid and CPR before providing direct care. §2800.69: 4 hours dementia training within 30 days of hire, 2 hours annually.
issues.fix: Replace 'not verified' with the figures above. Add paid pre-service training hours per hire (18 hrs x wage x turnover) and CPR/first-aid certification cost to payroll/opex.

issues.current: A direct care staff person age 21 or older must be present in the residence... Pro Forma models 730 hours/month
issues.correct: Direct care staff on duty must also be awake at all times, so there are no sleep shifts. The 21+ person may be the administrator only if the administrator provides direct care. Awake-staff coverage must be maintained across all buildings on the premises.
issues.evidence: §2800.58: "Direct care staff persons on duty in the residence shall be awake at all times." §2800.57(a); §2800.59.
issues.fix: Add 'Staff must be awake at all times (§2800.58)' to the task instructions and to the staffing notes. No sleep-shift discount is allowed.

issues.correct: The $500 unlicensed-operation penalty and the additional $20 per resident per day after 14 days are in §2800.262(g), not §2800.11. The amounts and the 14-day period are correct.
issues.evidence: §2800.262(g): "a penalty of $500 will be assessed. After 14 days... an additional $20 for each resident for each day".
issues.fix: Change the cite to '55 Pa. Code §2800.11(b) (inspection before opening); §2800.262(g) (penalty)'.

issues.current: The $85 allowance under 55 Pa. Code §2600.25a comes from a secondary source only... allowance and mechanics were not verified from DHS
issues.correct: The $85 PNA is verified in the official Pa. Code (§2600.25a, statement of policy). The charge cap is also verified: for ALRs, charges may not exceed the SSI resident's actual monthly income reduced by the current personal needs allowance (§2800.27(a)). DHS guidance also states the $639.30 PCH supplement and the $85 PNA. Note §2600.25a is written for personal care homes, so ALR use of $85 follows via §2800.25(c)(1) and §2800.27(a) 'current personal needs allowance'.
issues.evidence: §2600.25a: "The personal needs allowance for residents of personal care homes who receive Supplemental Security Income is $85." DHS guide: "PCH Supplement... (currently $639.30 monthly)... PNA of $85 monthly".
issues.fix: Update the notes to cite §2600.25a, §2800.27(a) and the DHS SSI/PCH Supplement guide as the primary sources. Add that SSI residents must receive hygiene items, laundry and ADL/IADL assistance at no charge beyond that amount (§2800.27(d)); this cost is not modeled.

issues.correct: SSA's 2026 table lists $1,633.30 for the 'personal care boarding home' category. The DHS guide verifies the $639.30 supplement only for residents of licensed personal care homes. I could not find a primary source confirming the same supplement for ALR residents.
issues.evidence: SSA: "paid to residents of domiciliary care homes and personal care boarding homes". DHS guide: individuals "residing in licensed PCHs are also eligible".
issues.fix: Mark ALR eligibility for the supplement as unverifiable and confirm with BHSL/SSA before modeling SSI-level residents in an ALR. Dual-licensed PCH/ALR operations are the clearer path (§2800.11(g)).

issues.current: Fire alarm monitoring, extinguisher and system inspections $100/mo fixed
issues.correct: Recurring mandatory items are not itemized. Fire safety approval must be renewed at least every 3 years. A fire safety expert must inspect and conduct a fire drill annually. Extinguishers need an annual inspection, furnaces an annual inspection, and smoke detectors monthly testing. Fire alarms must be connected to the fire department or a 24-hour monitoring service where five or more residents have mobility needs. Quarterly coliform water tests are required if not on public water.
issues.fix: Add a note and budget for the 3-year fire safety approval renewal, annual fire-safety-expert inspection, furnace inspection and, if applicable, quarterly water testing. Cost amounts are unverifiable.

The BHSL HQ phone 717-783-3670 and email ra-pwarlheadquarters@pa.gov are verified. Address: 555 Walnut Street, Forum Place 6th Floor, Harrisburg, PA 17101.
